narr: A frontal boundary swung into the Central Appalachians on July 12th and interrupted quiet weather provided by high pressure the day prior. Initially, showers and storms evolved along the front across Ohio and then spread eastward into West Virginia that afternoon and evening. Strong winds, large hail, and heavy downpours encompassed these showers and storms, leading to instances of tree damage and high water issues across the state.
ev: Teays Valley Road was briefly closed due to high water near the BP Gas Station. High water was also observed in Teays Valley at Mount Vernon Road. The Dairy Queen in Nitro was also flooded for a brief period of time.

High water was observed along a few local roads near St. Albans including Weiner Avenue and Kanawha Terrace. In the town of Tornado, Euclid Drive and Smith Creek Road were flooded as well as the road heading up toward the Big Bend Golf Course. Peyton Avenue in Indian was also flooded for a brief period of time. Standing water was also observed along the northbound lane of Interstate 77 in downtown Charleston.

East of Charleston, high water was observed in several areas, including Georges Creek Drive and Malden Drive in the town of Malden. Standing water was also observed on the 35th Street Bridge heading into Kanawha City from Interstate 64.
High water was observed along Klaus Street and Hartley Avenue in the residential area of Beckley.
An apartment complex in the suburbs of Beckley became inundated by high water for a brief period of time.
Flash flooding isolated and/or damaged 40 to 45 homes and washed out road shoulders, a culvert and undermined parts of several roads in the communities of War, Warriormine and Berwind.
